subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Considering the 'cultural context' of an artwork means thinking about...
options: Just the size of the canvas
The time, place and society in which it was made
questions.explain: Cultural context considers the historical period, place and society that shaped the artwork.

questions.q: Cubism is most associated with which two artists?
questions.explain: Cubism was pioneered by Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque in the early 20th century.

questions.q: Impressionism is best known for...
options: Capturing fleeting light and everyday scenes with loose brushwork
questions.explain: Impressionists used loose, visible brushstrokes to capture changing light and ordinary moments.

questions.q: Fauvism, led by Henri Matisse, is best known for...
options: Wild, bold and non-naturalistic use of colour
questions.explain: The Fauves, led by Matisse, used vivid, expressive colour that broke from realistic depiction.

questions.q: A 'personal response' (final outcome) should...
options: Bring together your research and development into your own resolved piece
Be unrelated to your earlier work
questions.explain: A personal response resolves your investigations and development into your own meaningful final outcome.

questions.q: When you give your personal 'interpretation' of an artwork, you are explaining...
options: What you think it means or communicates
questions.explain: Interpretation offers your view of the meaning, message or mood the artwork conveys.

questions.q: Surrealism aimed to explore...
options: The dream world and the unconscious mind
questions.explain: Surrealism drew on dreams and the unconscious to create strange, irrational imagery.

questions.q: Which artist is closely linked to Impressionism?
questions.explain: Claude Monet was a founder of Impressionism, famous for paintings such as his water lilies.

questions.q: When analysing an artwork, which is the best opening focus?
options: How long it took to frame
What you can see and how the formal elements are used
questions.explain: Good analysis starts by describing what you see and how line, colour, tone and composition are used.

questions.q: Vincent van Gogh is associated with which movement, known for expressive colour and brushwork?
questions.explain: Van Gogh was a Post-Impressionist, using bold colour and energetic brushstrokes to convey emotion.

questions.q: Which assessment objective involves responding to the work of other artists?
options: Developing ideas through investigation of sources
questions.explain: Developing ideas requires investigating sources, including the work of relevant artists and cultures.

questions.q: The 'Op Art' movement, associated with Bridget Riley, explores...
options: Optical illusions and visual movement through pattern
questions.explain: Op Art uses precise patterns and contrast to create optical illusions of movement and vibration.

questions.q: Salvador Dali is associated with which art movement?
questions.explain: Salvador Dali was a leading Surrealist, known for dream-like works such as his melting clocks.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'annotation' in a sketchbook?
options: To fill empty space with decoration
To explain your thinking, choices and development in words
To list the cost of materials
questions.explain: Annotation uses written notes to explain your ideas, decisions and how your work is developing.

questions.q: Which artist is most associated with Pop Art and images of soup cans?
questions.explain: Andy Warhol was a leading Pop Art figure, famous for his Campbell's soup can images.

questions.q: Abstract Expressionism is characterised by...
questions.explain: Abstract Expressionism used large-scale, energetic, often non-figurative gestural marks.

questions.q: Roy Lichtenstein's Pop Art is recognisable for its use of...
questions.explain: Lichtenstein imitated comic-book printing, using bold outlines and Ben-Day dots.

questions.q: Which artist created the famous ceiling of the Sistine Chapel during the Renaissance?
questions.explain: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling, a masterpiece of the Italian Renaissance.

questions.q: The Renaissance saw a renewed interest in...
questions.explain: Renaissance artists revived classical ideals and developed realism and linear perspective.

questions.q: Frida Kahlo is best known for her...
questions.explain: Frida Kahlo is famous for intense, symbolic self-portraits drawing on her life and Mexican culture.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock is famous for which technique?
options: Dripping and pouring paint onto canvas
questions.explain: Jackson Pollock developed a 'drip' technique, pouring paint onto canvas laid on the floor.

questions.q: In GCSE Art, the assessment objective about 'recording' asks you to...
options: Write an essay with no images
Record ideas, observations and insights relevant to your intentions
questions.explain: The recording objective is about capturing observations and ideas, for example through drawing and photography.
